output.brief: The stops are caused by an interaction. Firmware 6.4 keeps weak short-range returns that 6.3 discarded. The new glossy stretch film, in use since early August, produces those returns at oblique angles. Neither change alone does it. In the bench test, 6.4 with gloss film stopped 17 of 20 passes. The other three combinations stopped 0 or 1 of 20. The same split shows on the floor. Upgraded pallet robots in Zones A/B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 hours. The eight robots still on 6.3 stayed flat, working the same zones. Tote robots on 6.4 in Zone C, where no wrapped pallets are staged, stayed flat. That also rules out the agency temps as the driver, so the three-strike policy would punish the wrong people. Shortening the protective fields would cut a safety margin without fixing the cause. The December release is untested against this film, so don't rely on it yet. Next steps: call off the previous matte film from Northmoor (three working days) and keep firmware as is. Track stops weekly by zone and firmware group. Raise the film conflict with Halvane. I'm fairly confident. I did not check whether the stops caused the missed cut-offs, and the 18% volume rise also contributes to those.
